title: Request Orchard Sketches and Priority Inklings (Nov 2029)
body:
Purpose: compact working log that synthesizes customer-reported quirks and bundles small, testable feature probes we can ship in 1–3 sprints. Audience: CS leads, product owners for hosted-api & dedicated, solutions eng. This is deliberately lightweight — treat as a running experiment ledger rather than a final roadmap.

Topline signal themes (raw):
- Unexpected latency tail on short prompts when using the default batching config (Enterprise customers A, C).
- Confusing model-variant naming during automated fallbacks; customers accidentally hit higher-cost quantized variants (Customer E quote: "We upgraded flow and suddenly costs jumped; unclear why fallback chose that model").
- Request for per-route KV-cache metrics and a simple on/off toggle for prefix caching in Console (three mid-market customers).
- Embedding drift: customers see embedding similarity regressions after model upgrades; want a stable embedding alias and shadow-compare capability.

Quirk taxonomy (quick):
- Operational surprises (cost/latency regressions tied to fallback/model pinning)
- Visibility gaps (missing per-route/prompt-level telemetry)
- UX confusions (naming/rollout ambiguity in Console and API)
- Quality drift (evals + embedding changes)

Hypotheses and implications:
1) Latency tail is driven by mixed small/large sequence batches and an aggressive batching timeout; reducing max batch_wait_ms should cut tail but increase small-request cost. Implication: need an opt-in low-latency policy per-route.
2) Fallback naming + variant mapping is a discoverability problem — customers assume fallback stays within same cost tier. Implication: Console needs an explicit fallback-preview and a cost delta badge.
3) Embedding drift requests show customers prefer stable aliases + canary shadow evaluation before model swaps. Implication: add alias + shadow-compare to hosting flows.

Proposed micro-probes (ranked by expected signal / effort):
A. Low-latency policy toggle (L0 probe) — per-route toggle to apply low-latency config (smaller batches, shorter wait).
   - Owner: Marcus Chen (solutions eng)
   - Timeline: 1 sprint (spike + UI toggle)
   - Success metric: 30% drop in 95th pct latency for toggled routes in pilot accounts, <10% increase in token cost
   - Risks: cost pushback; require clear messaging

B. Fallback-preview UI + cost delta badge (L1 probe)
   - Owner: Leah Gomez (product-console)
   - Timeline: 2 sprints (backend mapping + small UI)
   - Success metric: reduction in "unexpected cost" tickets by 50% among pilot users post-launch
   - Quick test: build a mockup and run a 1-week usability session with 5 customer admins

C. Embedding alias + shadow-compare flow (L2 probe)
   - Owner: Tomás Rivera (applied-ml)
   - Timeline: 2–3 sprints (backend + eval harness)
   - Success metric: customers adopt alias for >60% of embedding endpoints in 30 days and false-positive regressions detected by shadow compare <5%

Quick patches (fast, <3d):
- Add an FAQ snippet to Console help about fallback tiers & cost implications (owner: Leah).
- Lightweight analytics dashboard card showing per-route batch wait distribution (owner: Sofia).
- Template support note for CSMs explaining embedding alias strategy and recommended rollout checklist (owner: Aisha).

Customer vignettes (raw notes):
- Customer A (fintech): intermittent spikes in 99th pct latency disrupted synchronous UI workflows; they reduced concurrency to mitigate — want an infra-friendly option instead.
- Customer E (marketplace): rolled out auto-fallback; saw 2x cost increase overnight; accused billing error.
- Customer M (platform): wants shadowing for embeddings during model upgrades — willing to be pilot.

Metrics to track for probes:
- 95th / 99th pct latency by route (pre/post toggle)
- Tokens per request and cost per 1k tokens by route
- Fallback activation rate and cost delta per activation
- Embedding similarity drift scores on canonical test set

Next actions (immediate):
- [Aisha] Draft short pilot invite for 3 customers (A, M, E) describing low-latency toggle and embedding shadow (Due: 2029-11-12).
- [Marcus] Spike a prototype low-latency policy toggle against staging runtime (Due: 2029-11-15).
- [Leah] Quick mockup of fallback-preview UI and a one-pager for CSMs (Due: 2029-11-14).
- [Tomás] Prepare a small embedding shadow harness and test on M's canonical dataset (Due: 2029-11-21).

Open questions / risks:
- Can we instrument batch_wait_ms and per-request batch sizes without adding high cardinality metrics? (SRE ask)
- Will dedicated customers expect different defaults? Need to decide policy scope (hosted vs dedicated).
- Billing UX: how to present cost delta so it’s not alarming but still transparent.

Notes / references:
- See Slack thread #cs-field-notes (2029-11-04) for verbatim customer quotes.
- Related backlog tickets: CS-4821 (latency tail investigation), REDW-8892 (fallback mapping audit).

Appendix: quick mock checklist for a pilot run:
- Identify pilot accounts + CS point of contact
- Baseline metrics 7-day window (latency, tokens, cost)
- Deploy toggle in staging, run 48h A/B experiment
- Collect qualitative feedback from admin users on clarity + cost messaging
- Decide go/no-go + follow-up plan

Bottom line: these are lower-risk, high-signal small experiments that tackle the most recurring friction (surprise cost + latency tails + visibility). Prioritize the low-latency toggle and fallback-preview UI first; embed aliasing is slightly higher effort but important for mid-term trust.
